episode_title: 636: Founder Friday! w/ Trevor Corlett of Madcap Coffee in Gand Rapids, Michigan

real_qa.q: Why did Trevor Corlett move Madcap Coffee from Illinois to Grand Rapids, Michigan in 2008 despite the recession?
real_qa.r: Trevor walked away from his previous cafe business in Illinois in early 2008 because he became increasingly obsessed with the producer side of coffee and wanted to highlight the complexities of sourcing through a minimalist approach. After becoming disenfranchised with the Fairtrade model due to lack of transparency and inconsistent quality, he moved to Michigan to start Madcap with a fully trained team of four baristas who had worked with him for two years previously, determined to make decisions with global impact through a focused cafe environment.
real_qa.requete: Madcap Coffee Trevor Corlett Grand Rapids 2008 Michigan

real_qa.q: How long did it take Madcap Coffee to become profitable after opening in 2008?
real_qa.r: It took four years for Madcap Coffee to earn a profit after Trevor Corlett opened the original location in downtown Grand Rapids in 2008, partly because downtown Grand Rapids was not a heavily trafficked area at that time with many empty storefronts.

real_qa.q: What is Madcap Coffee's approach to sourcing and long-term producer relationships?
real_qa.r: Madcap Coffee's sourcing goal is to establish win-win relationships with producers they buy from year after year, even during difficult times. Trevor states they have producers they have been buying from for 18 years and continue annually, with a commitment to purchase even when production is down or quality fluctuates due to events like droughts, embodying their core value of creating opportunity for others.
real_qa.requete: Madcap Coffee producer sourcing relationships values

real_qa.q: What was the hostile reception Trevor Corlett received when opening Madcap Coffee in Grand Rapids during the 2008 recession?
real_qa.r: The Grand Rapids Press published an article on the front page of the business section with an obnoxious photo of Trevor and the headline 'Does Grand Rapids really need another coffee shop?' at the time he signed the lease on the original downtown location that Madcap still operates today. Michigan had the worst economy in the country during the 2008 recession when he opened.
real_qa.requete: Grand Rapids Press Madcap Coffee another coffee shop headline

real_qa.q: What barista competition experience did Trevor Corlett have before and after starting Madcap?
real_qa.r: Trevor competed in his first barista competition in early 2008 at the Great Lakes Regional Barista Competition in Milwaukee, placing seventh while still operating his previous Illinois cafe. Nick Cho encouraged him to continue competing despite the low placement, and Trevor went on to have nine years of barista competition experience with back-to-back third-place finishes at the U.S. Barista Championships and winning the 2016 Eastern Conference title.
real_qa.requete: Trevor Corlett barista competition U.S. Championships 2016

guest.bio_context: Trevor Corlett founded Madcap Coffee in Grand Rapids, Michigan in 2008 and has been working in the coffee industry for nearly 30 years. He brings almost two decades of experience running a multi-location cafe operation with a roastery serving wholesale and direct-to-consumer customers, plus nine years competing in barista competitions including back-to-back third-place finishes at the U.S. Barista Championships and the 2016 Eastern Conference title. He has instructed with the SCA for 13 years, served on the Barista Guild of America board as chair, and joined the Coffee Futures Fund as a founding member in 2025.
